record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: In two dimensions, does there exist a local approximation theorem stating that every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian can be approximated on finite regions by a translationally invariant PEPS of finite bond dimension; can this be proved assuming only a spectral gap; and can the required bond-dimension bound g(ε) be chosen polynomial in 1/ε?

evidence.quote: Question 9 Does there exist a local approximation result in 2D? Is this possible assuming only the spectral gap assumption? Can g(ε) be taken polynomial in 1/ε?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a two-dimensional quantum lattice system on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space at each site. Let $H = \sum_{x} h_x$ be a translationally invariant local Hamiltonian, where each term $h_x$ acts on a bounded neighbourhood of the site $x$, and assume that $H$ has a spectral gap above its ground-state energy that is bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in the system size.

A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) of bond dimension $D$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is a translationally invariant tensor network state obtained by placing at each lattice site a tensor with one physical index (of the local Hilbert space dimension) and four virtual indices of dimension $D$, and contracting virtual indices along the edges of the lattice.

Question. Does the following 2D local approximation theorem hold? For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a bond dimension $D = g(\varepsilon)$ and a translationally invariant PEPS $|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle$ of bond dimension at most $g(\varepsilon)$ such that for every finite region $R \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$, the reduced density matrix of $|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle$ on $R$ approximates the reduced density matrix of the ground state of $H$ on $R$ to within $\varepsilon$ in trace distance (with constants possibly depending on $|R|$ in a controlled way).

Specifically:
(a) Does such a local approximation theorem exist in two dimensions?
(b) Can it be established assuming only the spectral gap hypothesis (without further assumptions such as frustration-freeness, injectivity of a parent Hamiltonian, or uniform local gap)?
(c) Can the bond-dimension bound $g(\varepsilon)$ be taken to be polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$?
artifact.status_search_result: The 1D analogue (locally accurate MPS approximation of ground states of 1D gapped local Hamiltonians with polynomial bond dimension) was established by Dalzell–Brandão (2019). In 2D, area-law results for frustration-free systems (Anshu–Arad–Gosset, 2021) and quasi-/polynomial-time algorithms for ground-state observables of injective/uniformly gapped PEPS exist, but a general 2D local approximation theorem assuming only a spectral gap, with polynomial $g(\varepsilon)$, does not appear to have been proved. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Locally accurate MPS approximations for ground states of one-dimensional gapped local Hamiltonians
status_evidence.snippet: Provides locally accurate MPS approximations with polynomial bond dimension for 1D gapped local Hamiltonians; a 2D analogue is not provided.
status_evidence.claim: The 1D version with polynomial bond dimension is known; the 2D analogue is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: An area law for 2D frustration-free spin systems
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a 2D area law for frustration-free gapped systems, but does not give a translation-invariant PEPS local approximation under only a spectral gap.
status_evidence.claim: 2D area-law progress is restricted to frustration-free settings, leaving the general gapped case open.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Quasi-polynomial / polynomial algorithms for local observables in injective/uniformly gapped PEPS.
status_evidence.claim: Approximation results exist under stronger assumptions than just a spectral gap.
